issue.title: fix: use generic NUT-17 subscription kinds
issue.body:
Refs: cashubtc/nuts#372

## Summary

Updates NUT-17 quote subscriptions toward method-independent kinds while preserving compatibility with current mints:

- prefers `mint_quote` and `melt_quote` when the mint advertises those commands
- falls back to deprecated `bolt11_mint_quote` and `bolt11_melt_quote` when mint info only advertises the old command names
- keeps deprecated `bolt11_*` subscription kinds in the public type surface for compatibility
- updates mint-info fixtures and websocket/wallet event tests to cover generic and deprecated command names
- asserts the multi-path melt quote test sends the expected MPP option without relying on a noisy negative request

## Validation

- `npx vitest run --project node test/transport/WSConnection.test.ts test/wallet/WalletEvents.test.ts test/wallet/wallet-init.node.test.ts test/wallet/wallet-auth.node.test.ts`
- `npx vitest run --project integration test/integration.test.ts -t websocket --coverage=false`
- `npm run api:check`
- pre-push `eslint '**/*.{js,ts}'` and format checks

issue.title: feat: add onchain mint/melt support
issue.body:
Adds onchain (Bitcoin) mint and melt support per [NUT-30](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/365).

## What's new

### Onchain minting
- `Wallet.createMintQuoteOnchain(pubkey)` / `Mint.createMintQuoteOnchain(...)`, request a pubkey-locked onchain mint quote
- `Wallet.checkMintQuoteOnchain(quote)` / `Mint.checkMintQuoteOnchain(...)`
- `Wallet.mintProofsOnchain(amount, quote, privkey, ...)` / `Mint.mintOnchain(...)`
- `WalletOps.mintOnchain(amount, quote)` builder

Onchain mint quotes are **locked to a public key**. The quote response carries `amount_paid` and `amount_issued` so callers can mint incrementally as on-chain funds confirm; a guard prevents over-minting a partially-paid quote.

### Onchain melting
- `Wallet.createMeltQuoteOnchain(address, amount)` / `Mint.createMeltQuoteOnchain(...)`
- `Wallet.checkMeltQuoteOnchain(quote)` / `Mint.checkMeltQuoteOnchain(...)`
- `Wallet.meltProofsOnchain(quote, proofs, estimatedBlocks, ...)` / `Mint.meltOnchain(...)`
- `WalletOps.meltOnchain(quote, proofs)` -> `MeltOnchainBuilder` (`.estimatedBlocks()`, `.keyset()`, `.privkey()`, `.run()`)

A melt quote returns a **single quote with multiple `fee_options`** (each pairing a `fee_reserve` with `estimated_blocks`); the fee tier is selected at execution time. The response exposes `selected_estimated_blocks` and `outpoint` once broadcast. NUT-08 change is supported on onchain melt.

### Supporting changes
- `MintMethod` extended with `'onchain'`; `MintBuilder`/`MintQuoteFor` updated accordingly
- New types: `MintQuoteOnchain{Request,Response}`, `MeltQuoteOnchain{Request,Response}`, `MeltQuoteOnchainFeeOption` (`src/model/types/NUT30.ts`)
- `completeMelt` now takes a `CompleteMeltOptions` object (`preferAsync`, `extraPayload`); the positional `preferAsync` overload is kept and `@deprecated`
- `MeltProofsResponse` now exposes `outputData`, so deferred NUT-08 change can be recovered
- `prepareMelt` config widened to `PrepareMeltConfig` (adds `nut08Change`)
- `SwapMethod.options` gains `confirmations`
- Onchain methods carry an `@experimental` tag pending NUT-30 finalization

### Examples & docs
- New interactive `examples/onchain_example.ts` (listed in `examples/README.md`)

### Tests
Unit and node integration coverage for onchain mint/melt across `Mint`, `Wallet`, and `WalletOps`.

issue.title: chore(crypto): deprecate verifyDleqIfPresent ahead of v5 removal
issue.body:
## Summary

- `hasValidDleq` gains optional `{ require?: boolean }`. Default `true` preserves the existing strict semantic (missing DLEQ on a v0/v1/v2 proof returns `false`); `require: false` accepts (NUT-12 "MUST verify-if-present"). Non-breaking on v4.
- `verifyDleqIfPresent` becomes a one-line wrapper around `hasValidDleq(proof, keyset, { require: false })` and carries a `@deprecated` JSDoc tag pointing at the new opt. Output identical to today's implementation for every input.
- The `hasValidDleq` JSDoc notes the v5.0 plan: default flips to `false` (NUT-12 spec semantic) and `verifyDleqIfPresent` is removed; the strict policy will be opt-in via `{ require: true }`.

The aim is to give downstream consumers an IDE strikethrough and a one-line migration target *before* the v5 BLS branch lands the actual removal.

## Test plan

- [x] Existing `hasValidDleq` and `verifyDleqIfPresent` test coverage passes unchanged (no behaviour change on the default path).
- [x] `npm run api:check` clean — `etc/cashu-ts.api.md` reflects the new optional parameter and the `@deprecated` annotation.
- [x] In an editor, hover/autocomplete on `verifyDleqIfPresent` surfaces the strikethrough and the migration hint.

issue.title: feat(model): add AmountWithUnit value object
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds `AmountWithUnit`, a unit-aware sibling to `Amount`, so multi-unit consumers (wallets aggregating across `sat`/`usd` or multiple mints) can do arithmetic and comparisons without silently mixing units. Binary ops require matching units and throw `AmountWithUnitError`; scalar ops preserve the unit.

`AmountWithUnit` and `Amount` are deliberately distinct types with no implicit coercion: lift with `Amount.withUnit()` or `AmountWithUnit.from()`, drop back with `.toAmount()`.

**Design Note:** Extending `AmountLike` to accept `AmountWithUnit` was rejected: that would silently strip the unit at every coercion point. CTS APIs continue to take `AmountLike ` and return `Amount`; `AmountWithUnit` is opt-in at the consumer boundary.

## Detailed Changes

- new `AmountWithUnit` class in `src/model/Amount.ts`: passes through Amount methods with unit checks as needed
- new `AmountWithUnitError extends CTSError`
- new `Amount.withUnit(unit)` lifting method
- updated documentation and migration guides
- tests bring `src/model/Amount.ts` to 100%

## Notes

No internal call sites migrated: `Wallet` / `Mint` / `SelectProofs` / `utils/core` continue using unit-agnostic `Amount`.

Public API additions:

- new exports: `AmountWithUnit`, `AmountWithUnitError`
- new method on `Amount`: `withUnit(unit: string): AmountWithUnit`
